en.statement: Svelte reruns <script module> when it creates another component instance.
en.explanation: Module-script initialization happens when the module first evaluates.

en.statement: A <script module> block can read variables declared in the instance <script>.
en.explanation: Instance-script variables stay outside module-script scope.

en.statement: Another module imports named exports from a component's <script module>.
en.explanation: Named module-script exports are accessible through the .svelte module.

en.statement: A <script module> default export replaces the component's default export.
en.explanation: Svelte reserves the default export for the component.

en.statement: The {value} attribute shorthand requires a matching variable named value.
en.explanation: Svelte expands {value} to value={value}.

en.statement: <Widget {...props} color="red" /> lets props.color override "red".
en.explanation: The later color attribute wins over the preceding spread.

en.statement: $state requires an import from 'svelte' in runes-mode components.
en.explanation: Runes are built into Svelte's syntax; importing them is unnecessary.

en.statement: Svelte's compiler rejects const make = $state; in a runes-mode component.
en.explanation: Runes are keywords of the Svelte language rather than values, so the compiler refuses code that assigns $state to a variable.

en.statement: A standalone JS module needs a .svelte.js name for Svelte to compile the runes inside it.
en.explanation: Svelte compiles .svelte, .svelte.js and .svelte.ts files. A .svelte.js module behaves like ordinary JavaScript except that it can use runes, which suits shared reactive logic.

en.statement: Developers directly increment a $state number to update its displayed value.
en.explanation: $state numbers use ordinary variable assignments.

en.statement: Mutating a plain-object item's property in a $state array updates dependent markup.
en.explanation: Svelte's $state proxies nested plain objects.

en.statement: $state makes plain class fields reactive when it wraps their instance.
en.explanation: $state leaves class instances unproxied.

en.statement: Destructuring a $state object's number preserves a live reactive link.
en.explanation: Destructuring $state captures the property's current value.

en.statement: Replacing a $state.raw array updates markup that reads it.
en.explanation: $state.raw tracks array replacement.

en.statement: $state.raw wraps its object in a read-only state proxy.
en.explanation: $state.raw creates no state proxy: it stores the object or array you pass as-is, whereas $state(...) wraps its value in a proxy with a different identity.

en.statement: A $state.raw array can hold separately reactive $state objects.
en.explanation: Reactive $state members retain reactivity inside $state.raw containers.

en.statement: $state.snapshot clones an object's own fields even when that object defines a toJSON method.
en.explanation: When a value has a toJSON method, $state.snapshot clones the value that toJSON returns instead of the original object, so a custom toJSON controls what the static snapshot holds.

en.statement: A .svelte.js module may export a $state number it directly reassigns.
en.explanation: Svelte rejects directly exporting reassigned state.

en.statement: In runes mode, $derived(price * qty) follows reactive price and qty.
en.explanation: Svelte recomputes the product from reactive inputs.

en.statement: $derived determines its dependencies before the component runs.
en.explanation: Synchronous runtime reads establish $derived dependencies, including helper reads.

en.statement: A $derived conditional tracks reactive values in its inactive branch.
en.explanation: $derived skips dependency reads from unexecuted branches.

en.statement: $derived.by accepts reactive state writes as part of its calculation.
en.explanation: Svelte rejects state changes during derivation.

en.statement: A dirty $derived recalculates when consumer code next reads it.
en.explanation: $derived recalculates invalidated state on its next read.

en.statement: An unchanged primitive $derived result still triggers its dependent DOM text update.
en.explanation: Svelte skips updates for referentially identical results.

en.statement: Variables destructured in a $derived declaration stay reactive.
en.explanation: Destructured $derived declarations follow the derivation's updates.

en.statement: In Svelte 5.57, a let-declared $derived value accepts temporary optimistic reassignment.
en.explanation: Dependency changes restore the recalculated $derived value.

en.statement: Mutating the object $derived(items[index]) picks from a $state array reactively updates that item.
en.explanation: $derived leaves the selected value as-is, so it stays the deeply reactive $state array's proxy and mutating it reactively updates the underlying items array.

en.statement: $effect runs while Svelte renders a component on the server.
en.explanation: Effects execute in the browser, rather than during SSR.

en.statement: An effect tracks state read later inside its setTimeout callback.
en.explanation: Timer callbacks run outside the effect's synchronous tracking.

en.statement: In the browser, $effect reruns after Svelte applies DOM updates.
en.explanation: A browser $effect observes Svelte's updated DOM.

en.statement: Svelte schedules separate $effect runs for simultaneous dependency changes.
en.explanation: Svelte batches simultaneous changes into one rerun.

en.statement: An effect's returned cleanup runs before its next execution.
en.explanation: Svelte tears down the previous run before restarting.

en.statement: A child's $effect.pre can run after its parent's DOM has updated in the same flush.
en.explanation: $effect.pre runs before the DOM updates scheduled after it, not before every DOM change in the flush, so a parent component's DOM may already be updated when it runs.

en.statement: During component setup, $effect.tracking() returns true.
en.explanation: Component setup runs outside a tracking context.

en.statement: Svelte's docs prefer $effect for a value computed from other state.
en.explanation: The docs recommend $derived for computed state.

en.statement: Awaiting tick() lets browser code observe pending Svelte DOM updates.
en.explanation: tick resolves after Svelte applies pending changes.

en.statement: onMount uses an async callback's returned function as unmount cleanup.
en.explanation: An async callback returns a Promise, not registered cleanup.

en.statement: Svelte runs onDestroy callbacks for components rendered on the server.
en.explanation: onDestroy also applies to server-rendered components.

en.statement: A child reads later parent updates through a prop destructured from $props().
en.explanation: $props() keeps destructured references responsive to parent changes.

en.statement: A $props() fallback takes effect when the parent passes null for that prop.
en.explanation: A prop fallback applies to omitted or undefined values.

en.statement: Reassigning an unbound prop in the child updates the parent's variable.
en.explanation: A child's prop reassignment creates a temporary local override.

en.statement: Mutating prefs.dark in a child updates its DOM when the parent passed prefs={{ dark: false }}.
en.explanation: Svelte's $props docs say mutating a regular object prop has no effect on the UI, because an object literal passed by the parent is a plain object rather than a state proxy.

en.statement: Svelte keeps the fallback in let { opts = { n: 0 } } = $props() as a plain object rather than a state proxy.
en.explanation: Svelte leaves the fallback of a prop declared without $bindable untouched, so the default object is used as written instead of being wrapped in a reactive state proxy.

en.statement: In development, a child's prop mutation can update the UI despite an ownership warning.
en.explanation: An ownership warning leaves reactive prop mutations effective.

en.statement: In runes mode, let {value=$bindable()}=$props() permits a parent to use bind:value.
en.explanation: The $bindable() initializer opts that prop into component binding.

en.statement: A parent may pass a $bindable() prop normally instead of using bind:.
en.explanation: $bindable() enables binding; the parent chooses whether to use it.

en.statement: A parent may bind an undefined value to a prop with a $bindable('draft') fallback.
en.explanation: A bound fallback prop requires a defined parent value.

en.statement: During browser hydration, $props.id() differs from the same component's server ID.
en.explanation: $props.id() preserves the component's server-generated ID during hydration.

en.statement: Svelte renders array-like values with {#each items as item}.
en.explanation: A length property lets Svelte accept an object as an each input.

en.statement: Svelte renders values from a Set with {#each items as item}.
en.explanation: Each blocks accept iterable collections.

en.statement: An {#each} block throws when its input becomes undefined.
en.explanation: Each blocks treat undefined inputs as empty collections.

en.statement: Svelte renders an {#each} block's {:else} branch for an empty array.
en.explanation: An {#each} else branch supplies empty-list content.

en.statement: A keyed {#each} keeps a moved item's index at its original position.
en.explanation: An each index reflects the item's current position.

en.statement: An {#each} header directly accepts item destructuring with object or array patterns.
en.explanation: Destructured names expose the selected item properties.

en.statement: A keyed {#each} can assign equal keys to separate list items.
en.explanation: Each key identifies its list item uniquely.

en.statement: An {#each} block can repeat markup with the as item portion omitted.
en.explanation: An {#each} repetition can expose an index while omitting the item binding.

en.statement: Svelte keeps existing components linked to their original items after an unkeyed {#each} prepend.
en.explanation: Unkeyed components keep their position and receive updated props.

en.statement: Changing a {#key} value preserves the enclosed component's local state.
en.explanation: Svelte recreates the keyed component, including its local state.

en.statement: An {#await promise then value} block lets a template skip separate pending markup.
en.explanation: Placing then in the opening await tag leaves out the separate pending branch.

en.statement: Synchronous server rendering waits for a Promise before choosing an {#await} branch.
en.explanation: Synchronous server rendering emits an await block's pending branch when its expression is a Promise.

en.statement: During synchronous server rendering, {#await 42 then value} renders the then branch.
en.explanation: An await block enters its then branch immediately for a plain value, including during synchronous server rendering.

en.statement: In Svelte 5.57, {const label = 'Hi'} is valid at the top level of component markup.
en.explanation: A declaration tag works directly in component markup, including outside a template block.

en.statement:
In Svelte 5.57, a declaration inside a
remains visible to markup following that
.
en.explanation: A declaration nested inside an element belongs to that element's markup scope; markup after the element uses the enclosing scope.

en.statement: For Svelte 5.57 migration, the docs prefer {@const x = y} over {const x = $derived(y)}.
en.explanation: For local-constant migration, Svelte's docs favor {const x = $derived(y)} and label {@const x = y} as legacy syntax.

en.statement: In runes mode, reassigning a plain {let count = 0} updates markup that reads {count}.
en.explanation: A template-local let holding a plain value is not reactive; declaration tags use $state, as in {let count = $state(0)}, when the value should update the UI.

en.statement: Svelte renders a string containing HTML tags in {markup} as escaped text.
en.explanation: Svelte stringifies and escapes ordinary text expressions, so tag characters appear as text.

en.statement: Svelte lets separate {@html} tags open and close a wrapper around ordinary component markup.
en.explanation: Svelte expects the HTML string supplied to one {@html} tag to form a valid standalone fragment.

en.statement: Svelte applies a component's scoped styles to HTML inserted with {@html}.
en.explanation: Raw HTML bypasses Svelte's scoped-style processing, so the component's ordinary scoped rules skip that inserted markup.

en.statement: A snippet passed to a child resolves captured variables in that child's script scope.
en.explanation: Snippets capture the scope where their declarations appear.

en.statement: A snippet's {@render} call to itself creates a compiler error.
en.explanation: Snippets may render themselves for recursive markup.

en.statement: A snippet parameter can supply a default value when the caller omits that argument.
en.explanation: A snippet's default parameter supplies the argument value when a {@render} call omits it.

en.statement: Snippet declarations can gather trailing arguments with a rest parameter.
en.explanation: Svelte rejects rest parameters in snippet declarations.

en.statement: Passing a snippet declared directly inside <Panel> requires a matching explicit prop attribute.
en.explanation: A snippet declared directly inside component tags supplies its named prop.

en.statement: The tag {@render (compact ? short : full)()} renders the selected snippet.
en.explanation: A render callee accepts expressions, including conditionals.

en.statement: Optional {@render children?.()} supplies fallback content when children is undefined.
en.explanation: Optional rendering produces no content for undefined snippets. An if block supplies fallback markup.

en.statement: Rendering one snippet twice creates separate markup instances at the two render tags.
en.explanation: Each {@render} call creates its own instance of the snippet's markup.

en.statement: A top-level exported snippet captures variables declared in the instance script.
en.explanation: An exported snippet cannot capture instance-script declarations.

en.statement: In runes mode, <View /> switches components when its reactive View value changes.
en.explanation: Svelte follows the current component value in the tag.

en.statement: An onClick attribute on a <button> handles the click event in Svelte.
en.explanation: onclick handles click; onClick handles a distinct event named Click.

en.statement: Svelte accepts onclick="save()" as a DOM event handler.
en.explanation: Svelte event attributes take functions rather than JavaScript source strings.

en.statement: A component callback prop receives payloads through event.detail by default.
en.explanation: A component passes callback arguments directly, such as save(value).

en.statement: A child forwards click handling by placing its onclick prop on a button.
en.explanation: The button calls the function supplied by the parent.

en.statement: The syntax onclick|preventDefault={handler} applies a modifier to an event attribute.
en.explanation: Event attributes use handler code for preventDefault; pipe modifiers belong to legacy on: directives.

en.statement: A click made with new Event('click') needs { bubbles: true } to reach Svelte's delegated handlers.
en.explanation: Svelte runs delegated handlers from a single listener at the application root, so a manually dispatched event has to bubble to get there.

en.statement: A native bubbling listener on an ancestor below the app root runs after a child's delegated onclick handler.
en.explanation: The native ancestor listener runs before the event reaches Svelte's delegated listener at the application root.

en.statement: In runes mode, Svelte makes ontouchmove event attributes passive by default.
en.explanation: A passive touchmove attribute handler cannot cancel scrolling with preventDefault().

en.statement: Svelte can invoke two separate onclick attributes on a button for one click.
en.explanation: Use one onclick function to call both handlers; Svelte rejects duplicate event attributes.

en.statement: The on function from svelte/events returns a function that removes its listener.
en.explanation: Keep the returned function to detach a manually attached event handler during cleanup.

en.statement: Svelte preserves valid numeric input bind:value updates as strings.
en.explanation: Valid numeric inputs produce numbers through bind:value.

en.statement: Svelte's docs recommend bind:group rather than bind:checked for radio inputs.
en.explanation: Radio inputs bound to the same variable with bind:group are mutually exclusive, and that variable holds the value of the selected radio.

en.statement: Checkbox bind:group collects selected values into an array.
en.explanation: Svelte collects selected checkbox values.

en.statement: Svelte stringifies object-valued options through a select's bind:value.
en.explanation: A select binding preserves option objects.

en.statement: Form resets restore bind:value from the input's defaultValue.
en.explanation: Svelte restores the input's declared default.

en.statement: Svelte clears bind:files when the bound value becomes [].
en.explanation: Update bind:files with a FileList.

en.statement: Svelte resizes an element through bind:clientWidth assignments.
en.explanation: Dimension bindings read measurements instead of changing layout.

en.statement: Svelte exposes DOM bind:this references during component initialization.
en.explanation: DOM references arrive after mounting.

en.statement: Readonly function bindings place null in the getter position.
en.explanation: Svelte sends DOM updates to the setter.

en.statement: createContext() returns get, set and has functions that work with the same component context.
en.explanation: createContext() pairs a getter, setter and presence check for one context.

en.statement: getContext(key) selects the outermost provider when nested ancestors use the same key.
en.explanation: When several ancestors provide the same context key, getContext returns the nearest provider's value.

en.statement: setContext and getContext can share an object reference as their context key.
en.explanation: Svelte accepts arbitrary JavaScript values as context keys, including objects.

en.statement: A component establishes its context with setContext from a click handler after mounting.
en.explanation: A component calls setContext during initialization, when Svelte associates the value with that component.

en.statement: A provider's local $state reassignment automatically replaces the object held by existing context consumers.
en.explanation: Context consumers retain the object originally provided. Reassigning the provider's local variable leaves that reference intact.

en.statement: Svelte creates separate component contexts for separate server-rendered request trees.
en.explanation: Separate server renders receive their own component contexts, so request-specific context values belong to the corresponding render.

en.statement: Svelte's docs recommend stores when complex asynchronous streams need manual subscription control.
en.explanation: Stores remain a documented choice for managing complex streams and controlling subscription or update behavior.

en.statement: A store meeting Svelte's contract waits for its next value change before notifying a new subscriber.
en.explanation: A conforming store calls a new subscriber immediately and synchronously with its current value.

en.statement: Svelte automatically manages a component's subscription when its template reads a top-level store as $count.
en.explanation: The $ prefix subscribes the component to its store and arranges unsubscription when appropriate.

en.statement: A writable store runs its start callback for the first subscriber and cleanup after the last leaves.
en.explanation: A writable store's start callback returns the stop function used when its subscriber count returns to zero.

en.statement: Svelte's scoping leaves the specificity of a component's p selector unchanged in the compiled CSS.
en.explanation: The generated scoping class adds one class selector's worth of specificity.

en.statement: Svelte adjusts component animation references to match its scoped keyframe names.
en.explanation: Component keyframes receive generated names, and local animation rules follow those names.

en.statement: The :global(span) suffix makes the div prefix in div :global(span) global too.
en.explanation: The div prefix stays scoped; the span portion matches across component boundaries.

en.statement: Passing --accent={color} to a component lets reactive color changes update its CSS custom property.
en.explanation: Component custom-property attributes accept dynamic values.

en.statement: Passing CSS custom properties to a component keeps its roots as direct children of its container.
en.explanation: Svelte adds a wrapper element, changing matches involving the > combinator.

en.statement: With class={{ active: enabled }}, Svelte adds active when enabled is truthy.
en.explanation: Object-form class attributes select keys by their values.

en.statement: Svelte can turn class={['a', ['b']]} into the class string 'a,b'.
en.explanation: Svelte flattens nested class arrays; this expression produces the class string 'a b'.

en.statement: Svelte's docs recommend class: over class objects for composable class values.
en.explanation: The docs favor class attributes for flexibility and composition.

en.statement: Bare style:color takes its value from whatever variable named color is in scope.
en.explanation: style:color is shorthand for style:color={color}, so Svelte reads whichever color binding is in scope, such as a script variable or an each-block item.

en.statement: A style attribute's !important declaration overrides a matching style: directive.
en.explanation: Svelte gives the matching style: directive precedence over the style attribute.

en.statement: Svelte passes the DOM element to the function used in {@attach setup}.
en.explanation: An attachment's element argument gives setup access to that mounted node.

en.statement: With make returning new functions, {@attach make(count)} keeps its setup as the reactive number count changes.
en.explanation: Svelte destroys and recreates an attachment when its factory expression produces a new attachment function.

en.statement: An element can use two {@attach ...} tags for separate attachments.
en.explanation: Svelte composes multiple attachments on the same element.

en.statement: A wrapper forwards a component attachment by spreading its received props onto a DOM element.
en.explanation: Svelte carries component attachments in Symbol-keyed props that survive spreading.

en.statement: Changing state read solely by an attachment's nested $effect reruns its outer setup.
en.explanation: Changes to state read solely in a nested attachment effect rerun that effect, leaving the outer setup intact.

en.statement: Svelte calls a use: action with a DOM node that is already mounted when the action starts.
en.explanation: An action receives the mounted node for DOM integration.

en.statement: A changed argument can make Svelte reinvoke an action on its mounted element.
en.explanation: An action runs once per mounted element; argument changes do not call it again.

en.statement: During server rendering, Svelte invokes use: actions to prepare the output.
en.explanation: Svelte invokes actions in the browser, skipping them during server rendering.

en.statement: Within a mounted component, removing an action's element runs its nested $effect cleanup.
en.explanation: An action's effect cleanup follows the element's lifetime.

en.statement: During an intro, Svelte reverses in:fly when it starts the element's out:fade.
en.explanation: Separate in: and out: transitions continue alongside each other during that interruption.

en.statement: Svelte keeps plain children in an outroing block until its transitions finish.
en.explanation: The block retains its DOM, including children that have no transition.

en.statement: A nested block's local transition runs when Svelte destroys its outer block.
en.explanation: Local transitions follow their own block; |global also responds to parent blocks.

en.statement: Svelte dispatches transition lifecycle events from the transitioning DOM element.
en.explanation: Attributes such as onoutroend on that element observe its transition events.

en.statement: Svelte accepts animate:flip on a keyed {#each} block's single immediate DOM child.
en.explanation: An animate: directive belongs directly on the element under the keyed block.

en.statement: Svelte runs animate:flip on the new element itself during a keyed list insertion.
en.explanation: animate: animates index changes of existing items, rather than the inserted element itself.

en.statement: The flip animation rotates keyed list items as they move between positions.
en.explanation: flip interpolates element positions through translations along the x and y axes.

en.statement: With default opacity settings, fly keeps a fully opaque element's opacity steady while it moves.
en.explanation: fly animates opacity alongside its positional movement.

en.statement: crossfade pairs sent and received elements using their matching DOM id attributes.
en.explanation: Pass the same key to send and receive to identify corresponding elements.

en.statement: The draw transition targets an SVG element whose interface includes getTotalLength().
en.explanation: SVG paths and polylines provide the length method expected by draw.

en.statement: In the browser, Svelte removes <svelte:window> event listeners when their component is destroyed.
en.explanation: <svelte:window> keeps its global listeners tied to the declaring component's lifetime.

en.statement: The <svelte:window> online binding reports whether the current application's backend is reachable.
en.explanation: <svelte:window> reads online from window.navigator.onLine, so the binding reflects that browser flag.

en.statement: Svelte scrolls the browser to the starting y value of <svelte:window bind:scrollY={y}> at mount.
en.explanation: Svelte leaves the initial scroll position in place; subsequent changes to the bound scroll value drive scrolling.

en.statement: Component code sets browser focus by assigning <svelte:document>'s activeElement binding.
en.explanation: <svelte:document> reports activeElement through a readonly binding; changing its bound value leaves browser focus unchanged.

en.statement: <svelte:body> supports a use: action applied to the browser's document.body element.
en.explanation: The body helper accepts use: directives for integrating behavior with document.body.

en.statement: A component places <svelte:head> inside an {#if} block when its title content is conditional.
en.explanation: Svelte expects <svelte:head> at component top level, outside surrounding elements and template blocks.

en.statement: When this is null, <svelte:element> omits its children together with the dynamic DOM element.
en.explanation: A nullish this value suppresses both the dynamic element and its child content.

en.statement: <svelte:element> supports bind:value whenever its this expression currently resolves to 'input'.
en.explanation: The generic <svelte:element> supports bind:this. Svelte's built-in value binding needs a concrete element tag.

en.statement: An imported child keeps its own component options when its parent declares <svelte:options>.
en.explanation: <svelte:options> configures the component containing that declaration.

en.statement: In the browser, <svelte:boundary> catches an error thrown by a button's onclick handler inside it.
en.explanation: A browser boundary handles rendering and effect errors. Errors from click handlers remain outside its error-handling scope.

en.statement: In the browser, <svelte:boundary> removes its existing content when onerror handles a rendering error.
en.explanation: Handling a rendering error removes the boundary's previous content even if it has an onerror handler and no failed snippet.

en.statement: Browser mount accepts a CSS selector string as its target option.
en.explanation: Pass the DOM target itself, such as document.querySelector('#app').

en.statement: Browser mount reads initial component props from the target element's attributes.
en.explanation: Pass initial component values in mount's props option.

en.statement: Browser mount returns the mounted component's exported instance functions.
en.explanation: Call an exported instance function through the object returned by mount.

en.statement: When hydrating, Svelte keeps a server-rendered src that differs on the client.
en.explanation: Svelte assumes src values match between server and client and keeps the server value, because resetting src could make the browser refetch the image.

en.statement: In runes mode, browser mount runs initial $effect callbacks before returning.
en.explanation: The first effect callbacks run after mount returns.

en.statement: Browser mount skips initial intro transitions by default.
en.explanation: Initial mount transitions play unless intro is false.

en.statement: Browser unmount with outro: true resolves its Promise as exit transitions start.
en.explanation: The Promise resolves after the outro transitions finish.

en.statement: On the server, render from svelte/server returns body and head HTML fields.
en.explanation: Use the fields to fill the corresponding document regions.

en.statement: With experimental.async disabled, server render defers body access until a Promise resolves.
en.explanation: Synchronous server render exposes its output fields immediately.

en.statement: SvelteKit supplies a filesystem router for applications built with Svelte.
en.explanation: The docs list routing alongside SvelteKit's server-side rendering facilities.
